name: Naousha
body:
Naous
CR 1/3

This slender bird resembles a black-plumed ibis, though with a striated pattern of bright, bloody red. Its neck is exceptionally long and thin, as is its curved beak.

XP 135
NE Medium magical beast
Init +1; Senses darkvision 60 ft., detect sentience 300 ft., low-light vision; Perception +2

DEFENSE

AC 11, touch 10, flat-footed 10 (+1 Dex)
hp 7 (1d10+2)
Fort +4, Ref +3, Will +2

OFFENSE

Speed 10 ft., fly 40 ft. (average)
Melee bite +1 (1d6 plus grab)

STATISTICS

Str 11, Dex 12, Con 14, Int 8, Wis 14, Cha 9
Base Atk +1; CMB +1 (+5 grapple); CMD 12
Feats Hover
Skills Fly +1, Stealth +5
Languages Common (can’t speak)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Detect Sentience (Su)

The naousha can detect the presence of creatures with an Intelligence of 3 or higher with a range of 300 feet.

Like scent, the exact location of the source is not revealed—only its presence somewhere within range. A move action can be used to determine the direction.

When such a creature is within 5 feet of the source, the naousha can pinpoint the source’s location. This sense penetrates through solid objects. The naousha can detect the age of creatures with the humanoid trait as part of this sense.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate urban
Organization solitary or pair
Treasure standard

This malicious bird dwells in cities and villages, hiding its nest on rooftops or high, rocky clefts from where it shelters during the day and remains out of sight. At twilight, it takes wing and glides stealthily over the city looking for open windows, as these intelligent avians have learned that small, soft prey is often hidden inside. Its cruel heart savors the piteous cries it leaves behind when it snatches a small victim and makes good its escape to feast.

When standing fully erect, a naousha can reach over 10 feet and a wingspan of nearly 20 feet, but it is agile in the air, often flying with its wings partly furled. It likewise walks in a sinister crouch across rooftops, its neck coiled and ready to strike almost like a viper, snatching its prey and then carrying it off to be devoured.
